answers.text: Give back three lines every time - drop-off time, pallet count, and damage noted - same order, same wording. If there's no damage mentioned, put 'none noted' instead of skipping the line.
List every call that needs a follow-up as its own line with time, customer, topic and outcome, and count those lines for the total still needing a call back.
The finish time is wrong - 8am plus about six hours lands in the early afternoon of the same day, the 22nd, not the 23rd as written.

96 to 118 is nearer a 23% rise than the 20% stated. And the balance being 'held steady' at €58,000 doesn't sit right either, given invoices went up that much - nobody explains why the balance didn't move.
Output 2 - it shows the 940 and 827 behind the 88%. Output 1 isn't necessarily wrong, it's just not possible to check without rerunning it.
Email 2, it has the real volume numbers in it. Email 1 doesn't give you anything to check the 'better rate' claim against.
The rates and retainer cap are sensitive, so I'd leave those out.
I check the reconciled totals against the warehouse count before the summary goes out at month end.

Step 4 needs the gate most since it submits automatically - I'd flag anything where the invoice and PO don't match within a small tolerance. Step 1 matters too, since a bad read there carries all the way through.
